findings.title: Crafted Symbol.toStringTag string triggers ReDoS in getObjectType
findings.description:
Entry: source/index.ts:245 (detect → getObjectType); the same path is reached by every getObjectType-based predicate, e.g. isHtmlElement at source/index.ts:666, isDate at source/index.ts:555, isMap at source/index.ts:717, isTypedArray at source/index.ts:914.
Attacker: a caller of this public API who supplies an untrusted object — e.g. a Node service that type-checks user-controlled objects with is(value), is.date(), is.map(), is.htmlElement() — crossing the library boundary from untrusted data into the type check.
Path: the object reaches getObjectType (source/index.ts:182), where Object.prototype.toString.call(value).slice(8, -1) evaluates to the object's Symbol.toStringTag, a string the caller controls, and line 184 runs /HTML\w+Element/v.test(objectTypeName) on that string before anything else.
Why nothing on the path stops it: there is no length limit on objectTypeName and the regex is unanchored, so for a tag such as 'HTML'.repeat(n) each of the ~n/4 'HTML' occurrences starts an attempt in which \w+ greedily consumes the entire remainder and then backtracks over it because 'Element' never follows; the total work is O(n²) (about 1.25e9 regex steps for a 100 KB tag, 1.25e11 for 1 MB). isHtmlElement(value) is only evaluated after the regex, so no structural check short-circuits it.
Impact: a single small object whose Symbol.toStringTag is a crafted repeated string stalls the Node.js event loop (or freezes a browser tab) for seconds to minutes, a CPU-exhaustion denial of service for any service that type-checks untrusted values with this library.
Fix: bound the tag before matching and anchor the pattern, e.g. `if (objectTypeName.length <= 64 && /^HTML\w+Element$/.test(objectTypeName) && isHtmlElement(value))`; the anchored form can only attempt a match at index 0, making the check linear.
